rationale: This additive Experience transport correction implements the existing Runtime-truth, bounded-read, and honest capability-state contracts without changing constitutional meaning. Large same-origin JSON responses are gzip encoded only when the client accepts gzip, retain exact decoded content and projection digests, carry correct Content-Length and Vary headers, and remain no-store. The Experience Gateway explicitly requests gzip from the Runtime while retaining the existing four-MiB decoded Capability Registry ceiling, strict JSON and projection validation, current-verification admission, one Registry read per bootstrap, child-read concurrency bounded to three, independent failure envelopes, tenant and workspace binding, secret exclusion, and fail-closed behavior. Full-scale tests use exactly 1,396 unique action records and verify gzip, identity, and explicit gzip rejection paths without truncating Runtime-owned truth. No generic proxy, mutation route, execution Authority, capability promotion, provider configuration, production claim, secret, data migration, or historical Mission record mutation is introduced.
